decisions.reason: Pushing HubSpot lists onward to MeetAlfred does not change the existing LinkedIn-to-Apollo-to-HubSpot ingestion path or its transfer semantics.
The candidate already requires seamless export of a follow-up list to MeetAlfred; the general HubSpot-to-MeetAlfred list capability does not alter its silent-lead recirculation or cleanup rules.
List synchronization between HubSpot and MeetAlfred does not resolve or change how existing CRM records are shown as duplicates.
The source decision does not address which LinkedIn or Sales Navigator URL is stored in the CRM.
The source decision changes list synchronization and does not alter the communication-history channels or their visibility in HubSpot.
Requesting HubSpot-to-MeetAlfred list synchronization does not change the existing test-account, campaign-preservation, or lead-safety policies.

The candidate's same-message Event already captures the independent instruction to integrate email with MeetAlfred and HubSpot; the list-push clause belongs to the source synchronization Requirement and does not modify the email-integration state.
HubSpot-to-MeetAlfred list synchronization does not change Apollo enrichment data or enrichment timing.
The synchronization instruction does not change MeetAlfred account setup or subscription-plan configuration.
The existing continuity Requirement already requires MeetAlfred to remain connected during integration work, and the source does not change that rule.
Although the source synchronization Requirement previously names Zapier as its integration method, message 359 does not change the Zapier account setup, plan, or add-on configuration.
